docs.title: mcp4api
docs.text:
mcp4api turns your API docs into a working MCP server, then calls every generated tool against your API and reports which ones work. The repository is smusali/mcp4api.

Built for platform teams who want their product callable by agents.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip install mcp4api
uvx mcp4api

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
These commands need no API key. They reuse the committed manifest and cassettes, regenerate the other artifacts in place, and exit 3. The sample's one known gap is get_book: page_count is a string in the API and an integer in the spec.

git clone https://github.com/smusali/mcp4api && cd mcp4api
uvx mcp4api examples/sample-api/openapi.yaml --offline --out examples/sample-api
cat examples/sample-api/report/verification.md

Where to go next:

  • Usage for every command, flag, and exit code.
  • Architecture for the four-stage pipeline.
  • Methodology for curation and verification.
  • Limitations for what mcp4api does not do.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
mcp4api SPEC runs four stages. Each stage reads the previous artifact and writes the next one.

flowchart LR
  Spec["OpenAPI spec"] --> Ingest["ingest"]
  Ingest --> Endpoints["endpoints.json"]
  Endpoints --> Curate["curate"]
  Curate --> Tools["tools.yaml"]
  Tools --> Emit["emit"]
  Endpoints --> Emit
  Emit --> Server["generated/"]
  Server --> Verify["verify"]
  Verify --> Report["report/"]

Ingest normalizes OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1, 3.2, and Swagger 2.0 into one JSON Schema 2020-12 document. The same bytes produce the same endpoints.json. Curate's input hash covers those bytes, the criteria prompt, the model id, the major.minor version, and the curation flags. A patch or rc suffix does not change the hash. It does rewrite generated headers, which is why the sample check accepts --update.

A matching hash and no --recurate skips the model. The base manifest is .mcp4api/base-tools.yaml when that file's hash matches. Overrides are applied to that base on every run.

Emit writes generated/ and .mcp4api-files.json, a digest of each file it wrote. A later emit refuses to overwrite a file whose digest changed. --force overwrites it. The published schemas are generated from the in-repo ApiSpec, Manifest, and Report models. Generated Python headers carry the source digest and a # noqa: E501 so the long line stays one line.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to this project are documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• mcp4api SPEC runs ingest, curate, emit, and verify on an OpenAPI 3.0, 3.1, 3.2, or Swagger 2.0 document.
  • mcp4api ingest writes a deterministic endpoints.json with every schema in JSON Schema 2020-12.
  • mcp4api curate writes tools.yaml with Claude, a local heuristic, or a hand-edited manifest, within a token and USD budget.
  • overrides.yaml renames, describes, excludes, restores, or fixes inputs on curated tools without editing tools.yaml.
  • mcp4api emit writes a standalone Python MCP server to generated/ and refuses to overwrite hand edits without --force.
  • mcp4api verify calls every generated tool behind a host allowlist, writes report/, and exits 3 on a known gap.
  • mcp4api record writes scrubbed cassettes from a sandbox, so later --offline verification needs no network.
  • The Shelf sample under examples/sample-api runs the whole pipeline offline.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Python 3.11 or newer and uv.

uv sync --group dev

docs.title: Checks
docs.text:
These commands stay offline and do not need an API key:

uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run mypy
uv run pytest

pytest disables network sockets.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
The documentation site uses the docs group:

uv sync --frozen --group docs && uv run mkdocs build

A GitHub Release deploys that version and points latest at it. Pushes to main update the dev docs.

docs.title: Demo recording
docs.text: tools/record_demo.sh rewrites examples/demo.cast and examples/demo.gif. It needs asciinema and agg. Run it when the CLI output changes.

docs.title: Curation
docs.text:
Agent mode sends endpoint summaries to Claude and asks for a tool plan, then for each tool's inputs and outputs. The criteria text is the system prompt. Untrusted document text is wrapped in delimiters. After the model replies, the code drops admin, internal, deprecated, webhook-management, and bulk-destructive operations, and any operation whose auth the emitter cannot express. One correction retry is allowed when the plan fails validation. If the token or USD budget is exhausted, the remaining tools come from the heuristic.

USD is estimated from the price table in the curation client.

Heuristic mode builds one tool per endpoint with the same exclusion rules and no model call. Manual mode loads tools.yaml, checks it, and applies overrides.yaml.

flowchart TD
  Input["endpoints.json"] --> Mode{"Curation mode"}
  Mode -->|"agent"| Hash{"Hash matches?"}
  Hash -->|"yes"| Base["Cached base"]
  Hash -->|"no"| Budget{"Budget left?"}
  Budget -->|"yes"| Claude["Claude call"]
  Budget -->|"no"| Heuristic["Heuristic tools"]
  Mode -->|"heuristic"| Heuristic
  Mode -->|"manual"| Base
  Claude --> Overrides["Apply overrides"]
  Heuristic --> Overrides
  Base --> Overrides
  Overrides --> Output["tools.yaml"]

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Verify emits the server, builds one plan, and calls every tool over stdio. The child process has PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE set. Fixture mode replays cassettes through a local server. Recorded cassettes drop request headers, and secret values are replaced before the file is written. --sandbox and --live dial the named host only when it is loopback or listed in --allow-host.

The generated client checks MCP4API_ALLOWED_HOSTS before a request. A local proxy checks the same list and records the exchange. A rejected host is blocked-by-allowlist and is not dialed.

flowchart LR
  Tool["Generated tool"] --> Client{"Client allowlist"}
  Client -->|"blocked"| Gap["blocked-by-allowlist"]
  Client -->|"allowed"| Proxy{"Local proxy"}
  Proxy -->|"blocked"| Gap
  Proxy -->|"allowed"| Upstream["Fixture or API"]

A call that fails is a known gap. A tool that passed only because the body was synthesized from the schema is still verified, and the report says the evidence was synthesized. A tool skipped by the write guard is not a gap. --on-failure exclude leaves the failed tool out of generated/ and still lists it in tools.yaml.

flowchart TD
  Calls["Planned calls"] --> Passed{"All passed?"}
  Passed -->|"no"| Gap["Known gap"]
  Passed -->|"yes"| Real{"Real evidence?"}
  Real -->|"yes"| Verified["verified"]
  Real -->|"no"| Synth["verified (synthesized)"]

The report fields are the schema in verification.schema.json.

docs.title: Built on
docs.text:
• MCP tool annotations: readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint.
  • Agent tool design guidance: one tool per intent, few parameters, hidden plumbing, trimmed outputs.
  • JSON Schema 2020-12 as the only schema dialect after ingest.
  • Record and replay cassettes for offline verification.
  • Seeded property-based example generation with Hypothesis.
  • Untrusted-text delimiters, plus exclusion rules enforced in code after the model replies.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: mcp4api SPEC reads an OpenAPI document and writes the artifacts under --out.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
mcp4api SPEC
mcp4api ingest SPEC
mcp4api curate
mcp4api emit
mcp4api verify
mcp4api record --sandbox URL

SPEC is a file path or URL. The primary command runs ingest, curate, emit, and verify. Each stage command reads the previous artifact from --out, so a run can resume.

  • mcp4api SPEC reads the OpenAPI document and writes every stage artifact.
  • mcp4api ingest SPEC writes endpoints.json.
  • mcp4api curate reads endpoints.json and writes tools.yaml.
  • mcp4api emit reads tools.yaml and endpoints.json and writes generated/.
  • mcp4api verify reads generated/, tools.yaml, and endpoints.json, and writes tests/ and report/.
  • mcp4api record reads those same inputs plus a sandbox URL and writes tests/cassettes/.

Paths other than SPEC are relative to --out. Flags may appear before or after the command. A flag that the command does not accept is a parse error.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
• --out DIR is the artifact root. It defaults to the current directory.
  • --json prints application errors as one JSON object on stdout.
  • --version prints mcp4api <version> and exits 0.
  • --quiet logs errors only. --verbose logs debug messages. Using both is a usage error.
  • --offline reads local files only. A URL, or a $ref that needs the network, is a usage error.
  • --allow-ref-host HOST allows a remote $ref from HOST. Repeat it for more than one host.
  • --model ID selects the Claude model. The default is claude-opus-5-5.
  • --budget-tokens N and --budget-usd N cap agent curation. The defaults are 200000 tokens and 5 USD.
  • --curation MODE is agent, heuristic, or manual. The default is agent.
  • --max-tools N is the tool-count target. The default is 20. Exceeding it requires a rationale.
  • --namespace NAME prefixes each tool name.
  • --include-tag TAG keeps a tag or a category. Repeat it to include more than one.
  • --dry-run prints a token and cost estimate and does not write tools.yaml.
  • --recurate curates again even when the input hash matches.
  • --force overwrites generated files that were edited after the last emit.
  • --deterministic omits started_at and durations from the verification report.
  • --live calls the spec server. A host outside the sandbox set needs --allow-host.
  • --sandbox URL calls that URL instead of the fixture server.
  • --allow-host HOST is a host the verification proxy may dial. Repeat it for more than one host.
  • --allow-writes calls destructive and non-idempotent tools during --live.
  • --isolate reruns verification inside a Linux network namespace.
  • --html also writes report/verification.html.
  • --on-failure MODE is exclude or keep. exclude is the default and drops a failed tool from generated/. keep leaves it and prefixes its description with a warning.

--json applies to errors raised by mcp4api. The parser's own usage errors stay as text and still exit 2.

{"ok": false, "exit_code": 2, "error": "not found: endpoints.json"}

Remote $refs are followed only for the input URL's host, plus each --allow-ref-host. A file input has no host, so every remote $ref needs the flag.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
• 0 means every generated tool verified.
  • 1 is an internal error.
  • 2 is a usage or configuration error, including a missing input. The message names the path.
  • 3 means at least one tool is a known gap. --json prints the same error object with "exit_code": 3.
  • 4 is an ingest, network, model, or upstream API failure.

--offline with record, --sandbox, or --live exits 2 before any connection. --live and --sandbox together is a usage error. A missing ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in agent mode is exit 2. --dry-run exits 0 after the estimate. --offline --dry-run exits 2. A file under generated/ that was edited after the last emit is exit 2 unless --force is set.

docs.title: overrides.yaml
docs.text:
overrides.yaml sits next to tools.yaml. mcp4api never writes it. It is applied to the cached base, so a second run does not apply it twice.

renames:
  list_books: search_books
descriptions:
  list_books: Search the catalog.
exclude_endpoints:
  - endpoint_id: GET /books/{book_id}/stats
    reason: low-value
    note: Stats are folded into get_book.
include_endpoints:
  - GET /admin/audit-events
fixed:
  - tool: list_books
    endpoint_id: GET /books
    param: limit
    in: query
    value: 2
    reason: hidden plumbing
outputs:
  get_book:
    - id
    - title

Descriptions, fixed values, and outputs use the tool name from the base, before renames. Renames do not chain. An included endpoint comes back as a one-endpoint tool. Unsupported auth stays excluded. Unknown names print stale override: on stderr and are skipped.

docs.title: Run it on your API
docs.text:
mcp4api openapi.yaml --out .

Agent curation reads ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. --curation heuristic does not. Commit tools.yaml and tests/cassettes/ when the same result should come back without a model call:

mcp4api openapi.yaml --offline --out .

generated/README.md names the environment variables. Add the server to Claude Code from the artifact root:

claude mcp add <slug> -- uvx --from ./generated <slug>-mcp

report/verification.md lists every tool. A known gap names the field that failed. Exit code 3 means at least one tool is a known gap.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
mcp4api is not a general code generator, an API gateway, or a hosted service.

  • OpenAPI input only (3.0, 3.1, 3.2, and Swagger 2.0). No HTML docs pages, runbooks, Postman collections, or GraphQL. An HTML page is rejected. Pass the URL of the OpenAPI document itself.
  • The emitted server authenticates with an API key or a bearer token from environment variables. An API key may be sent in a header, a query parameter, or a cookie. Endpoints that need another scheme are excluded and listed in the report.
  • The emitted server does not paginate, retry, or rate-limit. List tools return the first page. There is no problem+json parser and no MCP OAuth.
  • No repair loop. A failing tool is reported as a known gap and left out of the server. It is not fixed automatically. With the default --on-failure exclude, the failed tool is left out of generated/ and still listed in tools.yaml.
  • No PII redaction. The emitted server never logs bodies. The report's failure details include trimmed upstream responses, which can hold real data when you verify against a sandbox or a live API.
  • Python output only.
  • No hosted service and no GitHub Action. The exit codes are the CI interface. Streamable HTTP listens on localhost.
  • Agent curation needs an Anthropic API key. --curation heuristic does not.
  • Model output is not deterministic, so reproducibility comes from committing tools.yaml.
  • --isolate is Linux-only, and only when bwrap or unshare is installed. Synthesized fixtures are weaker evidence than recorded ones: the body was invented from the schema, so a pass does not show that a real server accepts the call.

Callbacks, links, and webhooks are reported as findings and are not part of the endpoint model. When a media type has both schema and itemSchema, the schema for the complete content is the one kept.
